title: Microheap affinity and ripple-eviction for paged-attention KV cache
creator: Morgan Chen
description:
Goal: reduce KV cache fragmentation and per-token prefill latency variability by introducing a microheap allocation layer ("heaplets") with kernel-affinity hints and a 'ripple' eviction policy that favors low-cost compaction targets. The design groups KV entries into small heaplets aligned to kernel-execution affinity and temporal locality signals (recent decode wave, tenant weight). Heaplets expose soft-reserve credits to reduce tail prefill stalls; when pressure spikes, ripple-eviction drains least-reuse heaplets first and incrementally compacts neighbouring heaplets to avoid large stop-the-world reclamations.

Scope: allocator changes (heaplet bookkeeping), eviction policy, kernel-affinity metadata propagation (kernel hint table per shard), decode admission/backpressure shaping (pacing envelope when reclaim under way), and an offline compaction worker to defragment hot heaplets. Includes telemetry and unit/regression benchmarks.

Metrics target: reduce p95 prefill latency by ~12-20% on mixed small/long sequence workloads, lower KV fragmentation score by ~25% in steady-state, and keep CPU overhead <6% on typical host.

Non-goals: full tenant rehoming in this iteration, cross-node live migration, and aggressive quantized in-place compaction (deferred to follow-up).
